content: The preferred empiric antimicrobial therapy for encephalitis involves administering acyclovir intravenously at a dosage of 10 mg/kg every 8 hours for a duration of 14 to 21 days. Specific Epidemiologic Considerations: 1. Agammaglobulinemia: Patients with this condition are at risk for infections caused by enteroviruses and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. 2. Age-Related Risks: Neonates: Common pathogens include Herpes simplex virus type 2, cytomegalovirus, rubella virus, Listeria monocytogenes, Treponema pallidum, and Toxoplasma gondii. Infants and Children: Pathogens of concern include Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Murray Valley encephalitis virus, influenza virus, and La Crosse virus. Elderly Individuals: Pathogens include Eastern equine encephalitis virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), and Listeria monocytogenes. 3. Animal Contact: Bats: Associated with Rabies virus and Nipah virus. Birds: Pathogens include West Nile virus, Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, Murray Valley encephalitis virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and Cryptococcus neoformans (via bird droppings). Cats: Associated with Rabies virus, Coxiella burnetii, Bartonella henselae, and Toxoplasma gondii. Dogs: Associated with Rabies virus. Horses: Pathogens include Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, and Hendra virus. Old World Primates: Associated with B virus. Raccoons: Pathogens include Rabies virus and Baylisascaris procyonis. Rodents: Pathogens include Eastern equine encephalitis virus (in South America), Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, tickborne encephalitis virus, Powassan virus (woodchucks), La Crosse virus (chipmunks and squirrels), and Bartonella quintana. Sheep and Goats: Associated with Coxiella burnetii. Skunks: Associated with Rabies virus. Swine: Pathogens include Japanese encephalitis virus and Nipah virus. White-Tailed Deer: Associated with Borrelia burgdorferi. 4. Immunocompromised Individuals: Pathogens of concern include Varicella zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, Human herpesvirus 6, West Nile virus, HIV, JC virus, Listeria monocytogenes, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Cryptococcus neoformans, Coccidioides species, Histoplasma capsulatum, and Toxoplasma gondii. 5. Ingestion Risks: Raw or Partially Cooked Meat: Associated with Toxoplasma gondii. Raw Meat, Fish, or Reptiles: Associated with Gnathostoma species. Unpasteurized Milk: Pathogens include tickborne encephalitis virus, Listeria monocytogenes, and Coxiella burnetii. 6. Insect Contact: Mosquitoes: Pathogens include Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, Murray Valley encephalitis virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, La Crosse virus, and Plasmodium falciparum. Sandflies: Associated with Bartonella bacilliformis. Ticks: Pathogens include tickborne encephalitis virus, Powassan virus, Rickettsia rickettsii, Ehrlichia chaffeensis, Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Coxiella burnetii (rare), and Borrelia burgdorferi. Tsetse Flies: Associated with Trypanosoma brucei gambiense and Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense. 7. Occupational Risks: Animal Exposure: Pathogens include Rabies virus, Coxiella burnetii, and Bartonella species. Horse Exposure: Associated with Hendra virus. Old World Primate Exposure: Associated with B virus. Laboratory Workers: Pathogens include West Nile virus, HIV, Coxiella burnetii, and Coccidioides species. Healthcare Workers: Pathogens include Varicella zoster virus, HIV, influenza virus, measles virus, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Veterinarians: Pathogens include Rabies virus, Bartonella species, and Coxiella burnetii. 8. Person-to-Person Transmission: Pathogens include Herpes simplex virus (neonatal), Varicella zoster virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (rare), poliovirus, non-polio enteroviruses, measles virus, Nipah virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, Epstein-Barr virus, Human herpesvirus 6, B virus, West Nile virus (via transfusion, transplantation, or breastfeeding), HIV, Rabies virus (via transplantation), influenza virus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and Treponema pallidum. 9. Recent Vaccination: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis may occur. 10. Recreational Activities: Camping/Hunting: Risk of mosquitoand tick-borne pathogens. Sexual Contact: Pathogens include HIV and Treponema pallidum. Spelunking: Associated with Rabies virus and Histoplasma capsulatum. Swimming: Pathogens include enteroviruses and Naegleria fowleri. 11. Seasonal Risks: Late Summer/Early Fall: Mosquitoand tick-borne pathogens, as well as enteroviruses. Winter: Influenza virus. 12. Transfusion and Transplantation: Pathogens include cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, West Nile virus, HIV, tickborne encephalitis virus, Rabies virus, iatrogenic CJD, Treponema pallidum, Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Rickettsia rickettsii, Cryptococcus neoformans, Coccidioides species, Histoplasma capsulatum, and Toxoplasma gondii. 13. Travel-Associated Risks: Africa: Pathogens include Rabies virus, West Nile virus, Plasmodium falciparum, Trypanosoma brucei gambiense, and Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense. Australia: Pathogens include Murray Valley encephalitis virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and Hendra virus. Central America: Pathogens include Rabies virus, Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, Rickettsia rickettsii, Plasmodium falciparum, and Taenia solium. Europe: Pathogens include West Nile virus, tickborne encephalitis virus, Anaplasma phagocytophilum, and Borrelia burgdorferi. India/Nepal: Pathogens include Rabies virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and Plasmodium falciparum. Middle East: Pathogens include West Nile virus and Plasmodium falciparum. Russia: Associated with tickborne encephalitis virus. South America: Pathogens include Rabies virus, Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, Rickettsia rickettsii, Bartonella bacilliformis (Andes mountains), Plasmodium falciparum, and Taenia solium. Southeast Asia/China/Pacific Rim: Pathogens include Japanese encephalitis virus, tickborne encephalitis virus, Nipah virus, Plasmodium falciparum, Gnathostoma species, and Taenia solium. 14. Unvaccinated Individuals: Pathogens include Varicella zoster virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, poliovirus, measles virus, mumps virus, and rubella virus. Specific Clinical Considerations: 1. General Findings: Hepatitis: Associated with Coxiella burnetii. Lymphadenopathy: Pathogens include HIV, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, measles virus, rubella virus, West Nile virus, Treponema pallidum, Bartonella henselae and other Bartonella species, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Toxoplasma gondii, and Trypanosoma brucei gambiense. Parotitis: Associated with mumps virus. Rash: Pathogens include Varicella zoster virus, B virus, Human herpesvirus 6, West Nile virus, rubella virus, some enteroviruses, HIV, Rickettsia rickettsii, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Borrelia burgdorferi, Treponema pallidum, Ehrlichia chaffeensis, and Anaplasma phagocytophilum. 2. Respiratory Tract Findings: Pathogens include Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, Nipah virus, Hendra virus, influenza virus, adenovirus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Coxiella burnetii, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and Histoplasma capsulatum. 3. Retinitis: Pathogens include cytomegalovirus, West Nile virus, Bartonella henselae, and Treponema pallidum. 4. Urinary Symptoms: Associated with St. Louis encephalitis virus. 5. Neurologic Findings: Cerebellar Ataxia: Pathogens include Varicella zoster virus (in children), Epstein-Barr virus, mumps virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, Tropheryma whipplei, and Trypanosoma brucei gambiense. Cranial Nerve Abnormalities: Pathogens include Herpes simplex virus, Epstein-Barr virus, Listeria monocytogenes, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Treponema pallidum, Borrelia burgdorferi, Tropheryma whipplei, Cryptococcus neoformans, Coccidioides species, and Histoplasma capsulatum. Dementia: Pathogens include HIV, human transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (sCJD and vCJD), measles virus (subacute sclerosing panencephalitis), Treponema pallidum, and Tropheryma whipplei. Myorhythmia: Associated with Tropheryma whipplei (oculomasticatory). Parkinsonism: Pathogens include Japanese encephalitis virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, Nipah virus, Toxoplasma gondii, and Trypanosoma brucei gambiense. Poliomyelitis-like Flaccid Paralysis: Pathogens include Japanese encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, tickborne encephalitis virus, enteroviruses (e.g., enterovirus-71, coxsackieviruses), and poliovirus. Rhombencephalitis: Pathogens include Herpes simplex virus, West Nile virus, enterovirus-71, and Listeria monocytogenes.
